summary: The user links two sessions on one backend with /link (one chat may hold many links; each is an edge). Agent sends along a link skip the one-hop limit and the per-sender budget and spend the edge's own budget (20 agent messages or 30 minutes, renewed by a message the user types in either session); sends anywhere else keep every existing limit. Auto mode sends along a link without a card. Stop or archive removes a link; links are in memory only. list_agent_sessions marks linked sessions, and the desktop shows a banner with the links and Unlink.

reactNativeIos.followUpRelease: mobile-v0.6.0. The phone neither creates links (out of scope by design: linking is a desktop action) nor shows the banner yet. Nothing unfinished is reachable: the React Native client calls none of the new channels and ignores the provider:peer-links-changed broadcast, and peer messages along a link render as the ordinary peer-message rows it already shows. The banner can read provider:list-peer-links, which is open to a chat-scoped device.

nativeAndroid.followUpRelease: Native Android 0.6.0. Same as the React Native client: no linking from the phone, no banner yet, no new channel called, and the existing peer.message rows render linked exchanges unchanged.

storageDataMigration.reason: Links live in the backend process's memory (PeerLinkBook in ProviderRegistry), never in SQLite or settings. A restart stops every session, and stopping a session removes its links, so there is nothing to persist or migrate. Peer messages along a link are stored exactly as before (same rows, same sender markers).

updateRelease.reason: No package identity, signing, deep link, update channel or wire-frame change. provider:link-peer, provider:unlink-peer and provider:list-peer-links are additive request/response channels; a desktop pointed at an older backend gets the unknown-channel error, which /link shows in the composer and the banner logs and hides. provider:peer-links-changed is a broadcast older clients never subscribe to. The PeerSessionSummary gains a linked field the model reads as text.

automated: tests/unit/peer-links.test.ts: link lifecycle (either order, relink renews, unlink one or all), an agent cannot link, a hub with three edges where workers are not linked and each edge has its own budget, budget exhaustion across both directions, window expiry, renewal by a human message in either session (all of a hub's edges when the user types in the hub), release on failed delivery, the third-session hop limit, stop/archive removal, banner text.

tests/unit/peer-links-registry-ws.test.ts against the real registry over WsHost: linking needs both sessions live and broadcasts provider:peer-links-changed; list_agent_sessions marks linked sessions; a hub fans out past the per-sender budget and a worker acting on its message answers it; workers still cannot message each other; a linked session at depth > 0 still cannot send to an unlinked one; 20 linked messages exhaust the edge with an isError refusal and a SEND_TURN in the worker renews it; a per-pair rate refusal gives the edge charge back; unlink one/all, STOP_SESSION and archive remove links; unlinking restores the ordinary limits.

tests/unit/mcp-peer-tools.test.ts: auto mode sends along a link without a card, still carded when unlinked, sandbox and accept-edits still carded when linked, plan still denied, and the server offers no link tool.
npm run typecheck and npm test green.
notExercised: Not run against live Claude, Codex or OpenCode sessions: no real agent pair was driven through a linked back-and-forth, so how each model uses the reply path is untested.
The banner and the /link and /unlink commands were not exercised in the running desktop app or covered by an e2e; the visual screens do not include a linked chat.
